subject: APAC edge + EU core tenancy split — architecture & cutover decision
messages:
From: HakuBank Ops <security@hakubank.com>
To: lauren_bishop@redwood.com
Cc: ops@tisglobal.io
Date: 2026-11-09T14:02:00Z
Subject: APAC inference edge + EU core tenancy — constraints and asks

Hi Lauren,

Thanks for taking this on. We are preparing our private deployment acceptance criteria for a multi-region topology and need to validate a few non-negotiables before we proceed:

- Key material (KMS keys) MUST remain in the EU — no replication of key material to APAC.
- Logs and persistent telemetry that include PII must be stored in the EU and never egressed.
- We can allow aggregated/metadata telemetry (request counts, error rates) to be sent to APAC for observability but only if anonymized.
- Failover behavior: prefer a warm-standby in EU (short failover window) — however, if the primary inference path is APAC edge, we need clear playbooks for when EU becomes active.

Could you outline recommended topologies (routing, peering, KMS placement, and data flows) and confirm whether Redwood can meet the key-material residency requirement while still running inference closer to APAC users? Also include any tradeoffs for latency and RTO/RPO.

We plan to share this with our security and compliance teams by next Thursday.

Thanks,
Arun Shah
HakuBank — Infrastructure Security
security@hakubank.com

Attachments: HB-compliance-checklist.pdf (attachment stub)

From: lauren_bishop@redwood.com
To: Arun Shah <security@hakubank.com>
Cc: marcus_lin@redwood.com, irene_choi@redwood.com, ops@tisglobal.io
Date: 2026-11-09T18:15:00Z
Subject: Re: APAC inference edge + EU core tenancy — constraints and asks

Hi Arun —

Thanks for the clarity. We ran through two pragmatic options and sketched an initial topology (attached). High-level:

Option A — Segmented tenancy (recommended):
- APAC edge: local VPC(s) hosting inference nodes (quantized model variants) that handle low-latency requests. No persistent PII stored here.
- EU core: separate VPC holding customer data, audit logs, and KMS (EU-region-only).
- Routing: application-level tokens and prefix/KV caching at the APAC edge. When a request needs PII or key access we route a tokenized request to EU (short blocking path).
- Keys: KMS lives only in EU; APAC inference nodes never hold unwrapped key material. Tokenization + ephemeral session tokens are exchanged to authorize operations that must touch PII.
- Peering: customer-managed transit (TGW/Transit) or private interconnect between the two VPCs with strict ACLs.

Tradeoffs: lowest latency for pure-text generation is APAC-edge; requests requiring PII will see EU RTT. Complexity: routing and tokenization adds operational surface but preserves residency.

Option B — Unified tenancy with egress controls:
- Single VPC with strict subnet isolation and egress guards. Easier failover but fails your "no key replication" requirement (unless we introduce a KMS proxy in EU which increases latency and risk).

Recommendation: Option A. Attached: redwood_topology_v1.png (topology diagram) and kms_keyflow_matrix.xlsx (key placement & call flow). Also attaching a draft cutover runbook for the segmented tenancy so you can review the rollback triggers.

Open questions for you:
1) Can you accept ephemeral tokenization (signed session tokens) for any operation that touches PII?
2) What is your RTO target for full EU activation if we fail APAC primary (minutes/hours)?
3) Will your legal/compliance sign off on the proposed private interconnect pattern?

If you prefer, we can set up a 30-minute tech review with Marcus and Irene tomorrow.

— Lauren Bishop
Director, Solutions — Redwood Inference
lauren_bishop@redwood.com

Attachments: redwood_topology_v1.png (image/png), kms_keyflow_matrix.xlsx (application/vnd.openxmlformats-officedocument.spreadsheetml.sheet), cutover_runbook_draft.md (text/markdown)

From: marcus_lin@redwood.com
To: lauren_bishop@redwood.com
Cc: irene_choi@redwood.com
Date: 2026-11-10T02:05:00Z
Subject: Re: APAC inference edge + EU core tenancy — constraints and asks

Lauren —

Quick tech notes (following your draft):

- Peering: prefer customer-managed AWS TGW with explicit route filters. Avoid over-permissive VPC peering; use prefix lists to constrain flows to only the token exchange endpoints and Kafka/RPC endpoints if used.
- KMS: enforce EU-only key material. We can use a KMS-proxy pattern in APAC that performs wrap/unwrap calls over an authenticated channel to EU KMS without persisting key material locally. This satisfies residency but adds ~50–120ms per KMS-bound call (depends on region). Suggest caching decrypted ephemeral session keys for very short TTL (2s–30s) only for throughput-critical paths.
- Telemetry: ship only aggregated metrics (prometheus counters, statsd) from APAC to our central observability; avoid shipping traces or payloads.
- Failover: design warm-standby in EU with pre-warmed model slices and cached KV prefixes to reduce cold-start. Full failover runbook should include: BGP re-route, DNS TTL drop, and application cutover with token re-issuance.

Action items I can take: produce a network ACL matrix (who can talk to whom) and a KMS call-latency budget for the team to review.

On another note — do we have any cloud-provider constraints from HakuBank around direct-connect settings?

— Marcus
Sr. Infra Eng, Redwood
marcus_lin@redwood.com

Subject: Re: APAC inference edge + EU core tenancy — constraints and asks

Lauren, Marcus —

This is helpful — thanks. A few clarifications from security:

- We cannot accept any persistent decrypted key material outside EU boundaries. The KMS-proxy pattern is acceptable if there is zero chance of key-material persistence on APAC hosts and if the proxy calls are logged in EU-only logs.
- RTO: our target for full EU activation is 30 minutes for critical user-facing paths. We can tolerate up to 2 hours for non-critical analytics pipelines.
- Direct-connect: we will manage the inter-region link — HakuBank will provision a private interconnect between our EU VPC and the APAC edge VPCs. That matches your TGW suggestion.
- Compliance: we will require a short attestation that logs and audit trails will remain in-region; please provide where those artifacts will be stored (S3 bucket paths or GCS equivalent) and retention windows.

We attached our acceptance checklist and a short diagram for the direct-connect setup.

Regards,
Arun Shah
HakuBank — Infrastructure Security
security@hakubank.com

Attachments: HB-compliance-checklist.pdf (pdf), HB-directconnect-diagram.png (image)

From: lauren_bishop@redwood.com
To: Arun Shah <security@hakubank.com>
Cc: marcus_lin@redwood.com, irene_choi@redwood.com, ops@tisglobal.io
Date: 2026-11-12T11:00:00Z
Subject: Final decision: segmented tenancy with EU-key residency and APAC inference edge (next steps)

Arun —

Thanks for the constraints and the RTO target — we are aligned. Summary and decision:

Decision (final): we will proceed with Option A (segmented tenancy). Main pillars:
- KMS: EU-only keys, no key material replication. APAC nodes call an authenticated EU KMS endpoint via a KMS-proxy design (no persistent unwrapped keys) and we will enforce short TTL ephemeral session keys.
- Data placement: PII + logs + audit trails stored in EU S3 buckets (bucket names will be provided in the runbook) and will never be replicated to APAC. Aggregated telemetry (counters/latencies) can flow to APAC after anonymization.
- Peering: use customer-managed TGW/direct-connect with route filters; Redwood will provide the ACL matrix and allowed CIDR lists.
- Failover: warm-standby in EU with pre-warmed model slices; targeted failover RTO: 30 minutes for critical paths. Cutover will use DNS TTL decrease + BGP path preference + token re-issuance.

Next steps and owners:
1) Marcus — produce the network ACL matrix and KMS latency budget (by 2026-11-16).
2) Irene — finalize the cutover_runbook_draft.md with S3 bucket paths and retention policy and share for sign-off (by 2026-11-16).
3) HakuBank (Arun) — provide final direct-connect topology and confirm bucket naming & retention constraints (by 2026-11-13).
4) Schedule: target pilot/canary cutover week of 2026-11-29; final date will be set after sign-offs.

Please review the attached cutover runbook (cutover_runbook_draft.md) and the topology diagram. If we’re good, I’ll produce a short attestation template that your compliance team can sign to confirm the residency commitments.

If that all looks correct I recommend a 30-minute alignment call on 2026-11-13 09:00 UTC — will that work for you?

— Lauren Bishop
Director, Solutions — Redwood Inference
